body.statement: The fully excluded finite categorical instrumental-variable model used by Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson represents a unit by an exposure response vector \((X_z:z\in\mathcal Z)\) and one arm-invariant potential outcome \(Y_x\in\mathcal Y\) for every \(x\in\mathcal X\), together with random assignment and consistency.

source.locator: Sections 2--3, categorical instrumental-variable model and response-function representation
source.verbatim_statement: Consider a categorical outcome Y with M at least 2 levels, a treatment variable X with K at least 2 levels, and an instrumental variable Z with Q at least 1 levels. For all the models we consider, we will assume the existence of potential outcomes Y(x=i,z=q) for i in [K], q in [Q]. We also define Y(x) := Y(x,Z) to be the potential outcome for Y arising from an intervention on X alone.

attestation.note: Verified from the primary arXiv v4 source bundle for Song, Guo, Chan, and Richardson, arXiv:2405.09510, notation.tex in Section 2; source downloaded from export.arxiv.org/e-print/2405.09510 on 2026-09-10.
